draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Tiruchendur! This shore town on the Gulf of Mannar is home to the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy Temple, one of the Six Abodes of Murugan, and the temple sits right on the seashore.
draft.hungryLine: Look out for chillu karuppatti, a candy you only get in Tiruchendur and around, and the boiled palmyra root (panangizhangu) that roadside vendors sell.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Start at the Subramaniya Swamy Temple on the shore, then walk about half a mile south along the sea to Avathara Pathi, around 10 minutes from here.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Stroll the shoreline between the temple and Avathara Pathi, where the sacred Makara Theertham is.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Tiruchendur means 'the Red land'. Legend says the sands turned red with the demon Soorapadman's blood after Murugan's battle.

spots.name: Avathara Pathi
spots.detail: 10 min walk · Ayyavazhi holy site on the shore where Ayya Vaikundar is said to have risen from the sea

spots.name: Manapad
spots.detail: 18 km away · Seaside village called 'Chinna Jerusalem', with an old church linked to St. Xavier

spots.name: Kulasekara Patnam
spots.detail: 20 km away · Old port village with the Mutharamman temple, famous for its Dasara festival

legends.title: The red land
legends.body: Locals say Murugan set out with Parvathi's spear to destroy the demon Soorapadman, who turned into a tree to escape. The spear split it into a peacock and a rooster, and the blood turned these sands red, giving Tiruchendur its name.

legends.title: Rising from the sea
legends.body: According to the Ayyavazhi holy text Akilattirattu Ammanai, Lord Narayana incarnated as Ayya Vaikundar and rose from the sea right here. Avatharappathi was built to honour that moment.

tips.title: Plan around Navarathiri.
tips.body: More than 1,500,000 devotees gather at Kulasekara Patnam for Dasara, with folk dancers from across the state, so expect packed roads.

tips.title: Dress for the temple.
tips.body: This is one of Murugan's six holy abodes, so cover shoulders and knees when you visit.

story.title: Murugan's victory
story.body: As the story goes, Murugan defeated the demon Soorapadman here, and his peacock and rooster came from that battle. The temple to him stands right on the sea shore.

story.title: A coast of many faiths
story.body: Ayyavazhi followers revere Avathara Pathi on the shore just south of the temple. Up the coast, Manapad's church is linked to St. Xavier, and nearby Kulasekara Patnam was once a port.

story.title: Palm country
story.body: The villages around town are red soil land, thick with palm trees and cashew plantations. That's why palmyra treats like karuppatti and panangizhangu are local favourites.
